name: Acetin Blue
lede: Acetin Blue is a dusty, greyed blue from Ridgway's 1912 chart, close enough to Denim that most eyes would call them the same.

sections.title: A blue from the chart
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 plate XXXV gives this hue the name Acetin Blue, hue 49′′, tone k, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files a close match in its block 204 [1]. Our sources do not explain where the name comes from, so its origin is undocumented here [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[alizarine-blue]], [[dark-cadet-blue]], [[indigo-blue]] and [[windsor-blue]], at 3.4, 3.7, 3.9 and 4.1 ΔE [1]. Its nearest relative in the library is [[alizarine-blue]], a brighter, more saturated blue from the same 1912 plates [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this blue in 150 of 23,781 paintings, 0.63 percent, as photographed [2]. The earliest dated match, Madonna and Child Enthroned by the Master of San Lucchese, is from 1350, more than five centuries before Ridgway recorded the name, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. It peaks in the 1920s, in 9 of 237 paintings, at 5.4 times the archive's overall rate, and Karl Isakson carries it in three of his 21 paintings here, far above his own museums' baseline [2]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a mid-tone, in 58 percent of its appearances [2].
